bullets.section: Autobiography I’m reading for the first time —
bullets.title: The Brotherhood of the Screaming Abyss
bullets.creator: Dennis McKenna, PhD
bullets.note: com/dennismckenna4?lang=en)). This has been on my to-read list for years. It’s a blast to finally dig into Dennis’s stories of family, experimentation, revelation, and life lessons.

bullets.title: Exhalation: Stories
bullets.creator: Ted Chiang
bullets.note: by** [**Ted Chiang**](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Chiang)**.** I’ve previously recommended Ted’s incredible collection of short stories titled [_Stories of Your Life and Others_](https://www.amazon.com/Stories-Your-Life-Others-Chiang/dp/1101972122/). Despite the fact that Ted started off as a part-time science-fiction writer with a full-time technical writing job, he is the equivalent of Martin Scorsese or Wayne Gretzky in the sci-fi world—he has won four Hugo, four Nebula, and four Locus Awards, among others. The hit film [_Arrival_](https://www.amazon.com/Arrival-Amy-Adams/dp/B01M2C4NP8/) ([94% on Rotten Tomatoes](https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/arrival_2016)), one of my favorite recent movies, is based on [one of Ted’s short stories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Story_of_Your_Life). Gizmodo [has written that](https://gizmodo.com/this-new-ted-chiang-short-story-could-change-your-life-1452465465) “the arrival of a new piece of short fiction by Ted Chiang is always cause for celebration and parades and wild dancing.” [_Exhalation_](https://www.amazon.com/Exhalation-Stories-Ted-Chiang/dp/1101947888/), his newest collection, may be even better than his last. It’s just ridiculously good.

bullets.title: The French Burglar Who Pulled Off His Generation’s Biggest Art Heist
bullets.note: ([_The New Yorker_](https://twitter.com/NewYorker)). After my previous mention of the [_Sour Grapes_](https://www.amazon.com/Sour-Grapes-Rudy-Kurniawan/dp/B06XWKJN5F/) doc in 5BF, my brother, who’d also read [_Billionaire’s Vinegar_](https://www.amazon.com/Billionaires-Vinegar-Mystery-Worlds-Expensive/dp/0307338789), said, “Oh, if you like that, I have something you’ll really like.” He sent me this _New Yorker_ piece. It blends theft and art in more ways than one.

bullets.section: Shop I’m excited to visit once again —
bullets.title: Fountain Pen Hospital
bullets.note: Now that I’m fully vaccinated, I’m excited to get back to the Fountain Pen Hospital, which was “founded in 1946 by Phil Wiederlight and Al Wiederlight (the father and grandfather, respectively, of today’s proprietors – Terry and Steve Wiederlight). Terry and Steve have a combined 60 years experience in all phases of vintage and modern writing instruments.” Special thanks to [Neil Gaiman](https://tim.blog/2019/03/28/neil-gaiman/?utm_source=convertkit&utm_medium=convertkit&utm_campaign=5bf) for recommending it during [our conversation together](https://tim.blog/2019/03/28/neil-gaiman/?utm_source=convertkit&utm_medium=convertkit&utm_campaign=5bf), in which he described how and why he does so much writing by hand.
